picks.title: 삼성전자, 갤럭시 워치 수면 무호흡 기능 고도화…FDA이어 식약처 허가 획득
picks.excerpt: 삼성전자가 갤럭시 워치의 AI 기반 수면 무호흡 기능을 고도화해 식약처 허가를 받았다. 징후 유무만 보던 기존 기능과 달리 시간당 호흡 장애 횟수로 경미·중등도·중증을 구분한다.
picks.rationale: A regulatory approval that reaches patients directly. MFDS cleared the upgraded Galaxy Watch sleep-apnea feature, which now grades severity (mild, moderate, severe) by breathing events per hour instead of only flagging signs. Medicine owns this story today, and it appears in neither the medicine 30-day history nor gadgets' published URLs.

picks.title: Who's responsible when clinical AI goes wrong? AMA weighs in
picks.excerpt: The American Medical Association released a new framework laying out how developers, health systems and physicians should share liability when clinical AI causes harm, building on its recent governance guidance.
picks.rationale: A new official AMA document that sets out how developers, health systems and physicians share liability when clinical AI causes harm. It is a separate release from the 10-16 agentic-AI governance framework, and it bears directly on clinician accountability.

picks.title: Accuracy and impact of an AI safety system for missed specialist referrals in primary care
picks.excerpt: Researchers built MR-AI, which flags missed specialist referrals in consultation notes, and evaluated it in a quasi-experimental study across seven primary care clinics.
picks.rationale: A patient-safety study run in practice: MR-AI flags specialist referrals missed in consultation notes, and it was evaluated across seven primary-care clinics. No referral-safety story is in the 30-day history.

picks.title: Development, validation and AI chatbot evaluation of the Adolescent Mental Health AI Response Tool
picks.excerpt: Clinicians built AMHART to grade how AI chatbots respond to teens disclosing anxiety or depression. Testing four widely used chatbots exposed gaps in how they respond.
picks.rationale: Clinicians built and validated AMHART, a tool that grades how chatbots respond to teens who disclose anxiety or depression. They then used it to expose gaps in four widely used chatbots. The 10-12 JAMA card on a cancer-risk chatbot for young people with cancer predisposition is a different intervention and a different study.

picks.title: Brainomix highlights AI study on stroke drug responders
picks.excerpt: A study using Brainomix's automated noncontrast CT analysis helped identify large hemispheric infarction patients who could benefit from intravenous glyburide.
picks.rationale: A treatment-selection result: automated noncontrast-CT analysis picked out large hemispheric infarction patients likely to benefit from IV glyburide. The AI is central to the finding, and no Brainomix or stroke-treatment-selection story is in the 30-day history. The source is a vendor-highlighted study, so the copy must attribute it.

dedup.note: DROPPED AS DUPLICATES / FOLLOW-UPS: Radiology Business 'Radiology societies weigh in on FDA's push to regulate generative AI'. These are comments in the same FDA genAI-device comment period as the 10-23 Healthcare Dive card (developers-not-doctors accountability), so they are reactions with no new decision. STAT 'FDA, CMS scramble... state sandboxes'. This is behind-the-scenes reporting with no new decision or release, on the running state-sandbox story (10-07 Utah pilots, 10-15 lobbyists). Story_dedup had already removed the breast-MRI recurrence clearance (same as the 10-19 SimBioSys card). NOT PICKED: Deep Reasoning NeuroDR FDA clearance, already rejected on 10-30 because the enrichment fetch found AI only in the company name. Counsel Health/LillyDirect, where AI is secondary to the commercial tie-up (same call as 10-30). SIIM-CAIMI Apollo, which would be a third SIIM-CAIMI conference card after 10-28 and 10-29. Coronary plaque CCTA overview (10-19, evergreen, stale). Nature Medicine EVLF-FM (a distinct model, but a second medical VLM card soon after the 10-13 open VLM; lower rank). 숨빗AI conference talk (a talk, not a release, and close to the 10-30 HOPPR report drafting). 용인세브란스 CXR-LVEF AI (a good runner-up, held back for outlet spread). Google Singapore health hub (a partnership announcement, close to business noise). CROSS-SECTION: the gadgets section of published_urls.json has no Samsung sleep-apnea/MFDS URL, and medicine owns that story today. The other picks are nature.com, fiercehealthcare and auntminnie items that appear in no medicine history. The curator had Read-only access and did not exact-grep science/marketing for the nature.com URLs, so the orchestrator should grep before roll. Diversity: 4 outlets (메디게이트뉴스, Fierce Healthcare, nature.com x2 [npj Digital Medicine, Nature Mental Health], AuntMinnie). No pathogen or biosecurity content.
